Your Guide
Benito Tush'ku
Mazatlan Villa de Flores, Oaxaca · Sierra Madres
Benito was born on Ka'jen — a sacred mountain in the indigenous Mazatec community of Oaxaca's Sierra Madres, where traditional medicine is not a practice but a way of life. His grandfather, a celebrated curandero of over fifty years, introduced him to this world early. That grandfather himself studied under apprentices of the legendary María Sabina.
At eleven, Benito was already at his grandfather's side during healing ceremonies. By thirteen, he had completed his first plant dieta — a threshold that marked the beginning of a life in service to the medicine. In the decades since, he has dedicated himself fully to facilitating physical, mental, and spiritual healing through plants, Temazcal, and practices passed down across generations.
What makes Benito different
He carries the full weight of a lineage that runs through María Sabina herself — yet shows up to ceremony with the energy of someone who genuinely loves being there. His nights often go until sunrise, filled with music, movement, and a kind of aliveness that makes the work feel like a celebration. Ancient roots. Living fire.
